chunk_findings.detail: The new path restriction is verified only when `edit.landed_paths` is supplied. If an item already has `landed_paths` and the operator later records or corrects the landing with `update --landed <range>` without also supplying `--landed-paths`, the `edit.landed is not None` branch records the new `landed_before`/`landed_after` and never calls `LD.check_paths` against the existing `landed_paths`. The item can then keep a path restriction that is not inside the newly recorded landing range, while `changed_paths` still reports only those paths; the doc-only pipeline can therefore run for a landing whose changed files do not contain the item’s recorded docs. Existing `landed_paths` should be revalidated, cleared, or the landing change should require a new path restriction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items.py:update (landed_paths handling)

chunk_findings.detail: When `landed_paths` is set, `changed_paths` can return an empty list even though git successfully reported changed files for the landed range. For example, with `landed_before..landed_after` changing only `src/x.py` and `landed_paths=['docs/y.md']`, `CH.changed_paths` returns `['src/x.py']`, but the filter returns `[]`. The function’s documented contract says it returns `None` when git cannot say and “never an empty ‘nothing changed’”; returning `[]` here makes a failed path restriction look like a successful empty change set. Callers that rely on the non-empty invariant and classify docs-only with `paths is not None and all(is_doc(p) for p in paths)` will see the empty list as vacuously docs-only, so a range that no longer holds any of the item’s restricted work can get the doc pipeline instead of failing closed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion.py:changed_paths
